summary: Comprehensive Expo web preview UI testing of File Mind (offline-first Android app). All requested screens render without crashes/white screens/red overlays. Home tab (brand header, search pill, 4 quick actions, storage card, recent empty state, suggested cards), Files tab (filter chips, FAB, empty state), PDF tab (horizontal tool row with Merge/Split/Images->PDF/Compress/Watermark, empty state with 'Scan a document' action), and AI tab (Files AI header, On-device/Offline badge, 5 suggestion chips, input, send) all render correctly. Bottom tab navigation switches between Home/Files/PDF/AI with orange brand accent. AI chat validated for 4 intent replies: search ('No files matched'), translate (honest 'offline translation isn't available' reply), merge (reply + 'Open PDF Merge' action chip), summarize (reply asking for a document / none indexed). All Tools screen shows all 6 categories (File Tools, PDF Tools, Scanner & OCR, Convert & Compress, Organize & Storage, AI & Security). Settings screen shows Theme selector (System/Light/Dark all tappable), support email jarvisai9077@gmail.com, and links to Privacy/Terms. Privacy Policy and Terms & Conditions render full readable text with header-back button present. Vault, Scanner (camera permission UI), Storage, Duplicates, Trash and Smart Organize screens all render on web without crash. Only warnings observed are benign React Native Web deprecation warnings ('shadow*' style props, props.pointerEvents).

react_native_issues.issue: Console shows 'shadow*' style props are deprecated (use boxShadow) and 'props.pointerEvents is deprecated (use style.pointerEvents)'. Benign for web preview; may originate from a shared UI dependency. Reference: browser console during initial render.

action_items: Optional: audit `shadow*` style usages and `pointerEvents` props in shared UI components (e.g., /app/frontend/src/components/ui.tsx) to remove React Native Web deprecation warnings. Non-blocking; only surfaces on web preview.

No functional fixes required. All requested test cases passed on web preview. Native-only flows (real file system, PDF viewer WebView, biometrics, camera capture, OCR) still need on-device validation via Expo Go / native build as per agent-to-agent context note.
critical_code_review_comments: AI intent handling in /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/ai.tsx is pure-JS and correctly returns honest offline replies (no fake translation). Good.
Home tab correctly uses expo-file-system/legacy and gracefully handles null documentDirectory on web (0 B storage rendered instead of crash).
All interactive elements use testID props that render as data-testid on web preview — testability is excellent.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (all 53 UI/navigation/intent checks across two browser runs passed; a single Playwright 'element not visible' error on Privacy back button was a test-driver quirk — the button is visible and functional as confirmed via screenshot and direct testID count)

seed_data_creation: None. App is offline-only with no backend/auth; empty states are expected on the web preview.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Frontend URL: https://app-runner-141.preview.emergentagent.com/. Mobile viewport 390x844. All screens use testID -> data-testid mapping. Key testIDs: quick-scan, quick-pdf-tools, quick-all-tools, quick-vault, home-settings, home-search, home-storage, home-empty-recent, filter-all, files-fab, pdf-tool-merge, ai-input, ai-send, ai-suggest, ai-action-<label>, theme-system/theme-light/theme-dark, set-privacy, set-terms, set-support, header-back. Direct-route navigation works: /scanner, /vault, /storage, /duplicates, /trash, /organize, /privacy, /terms, /tools, /settings. Native modules are intentionally stubbed on web — expect empty states for file system / PDF / OCR / camera capture / biometrics. Do NOT retest these on web.
